messages:
rachel: getting 429s on project 'alpha-web' around 2026-02-11 14:12 UTC, but the dashboard project tile shows ~250k tokens left in the rolling window. customer is on a demo call, urgent. any ideas?
liam: can you paste the exact request that got 429 and the response body? also which org id?
rachel: org=org-123. curl i used:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}'
```
response: `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit\",\"message\":\"quota exceeded\",\"meta\":{\"code\":429}}}`
jana: quick hypothesis: org shared pool enforcement fired before the dashboard aggregator ticked. dashboard tiles are per-project cached views and can lag behind org-level ledger enforcement. ops-bot posted an alert at 2026-02-11T14:12:07Z for org-123 enforcement.
ops-bot: ALERT org-pool-enforce level=ERROR time=2026-02-11T14:12:07Z org=org-123 project=alpha-web used=995400 reserved=0
liam: can you query the realtime usage API and ledger? `/v1/usage?org_id=org-123&window=rolling-1h` and check `/internal/ledger/ledger_tail?org=org-123` for exact debit timestamps.
rachel: did that — realtime usage shows org pool at 98% at 14:11:58, but project-level debit entries landed a few ms later. dashboard tile TTL is 60s so it still showed ~250k tokens available.
kevin: root cause seems to be timing/race between the enforcement path (reads ledger) and dashboard aggregator (reads aggregated counters with cache). if a high-QPS burst crosses the org threshold between aggregator ticks you can see the tile show capacity while enforcement denies requests.
jana: reproducible steps we used in staging: 1) create org with shared pool 1,000,000 tokens and two projects 2) start steady baseline traffic, then at T+30s fire concurrent bursts from both projects (each ~700 rps) 3) observe that enforcement returns 429 for one project at T+30:07 while dashboard project tile still shows availability until the T+60 aggregator update.
liam: customer-facing mitigation options: a) reduce dashboard TTL to 10s for tiles that surface quota, b) show org-pool live-utilization and last-updated timestamp on the tile, or c) change enforcement to do an atomic reservation check before returning 429 (safer but may add latency).
kevin: short-term operational fix — enable a small per-project reservation for org-123 (50k tokens) so alpha-web has headroom during bursts. i've opened infra changelist infra#4587 and will apply it after review.
support-bot: Incident created INC-2026-89 linking thread and infra#4587.
rachel: customer asked for steps to reproduce so they can validate; added the staging script and timestamps. putting them here in case SRE wants to run quick repro.
jana: also log note: aggregator runs every 30s with a 10s ingestion delay, and dashboard tile cache TTL is 60s by default. those numbers make the observed window where tiles are stale up to ~70s.
liam: to validate fix, we should add an endpoint return header when 429 is org-enforcement so clients can distinguish project vs org limit: `X-RateLimit-Reason: org_shared_pool` — will draft quick patch.
kevin: will coordinate deployment. if we want a higher-visibility quick win, expose `org_live_util_pct` on the project tile and add the last-updated timestamp.
rachel: thanks all — i'll update the customer and keep thread posted. :thumbsup:
